paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. The man at the gate asked for money, and Peter gave him something better. Peter said, "Silver or gold I do not have, but what I have I give you: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, get up and walk!" (Acts 3:6). Peter's power wasn't the point. Jesus was.

Then the crowd came running, and Peter wouldn't take a bit of the credit. He asked why they stared "as if by our own power or godliness we had made this man walk" (Acts 3:12). He pointed them straight to Jesus, the one they had rejected and killed, the "Author of life," whom God raised from the dead (Acts 3:15). And here's the good part. Peter says, "I know that you acted in ignorance," and then he invites them in: "Repent, then, and turn back, so that your sins may be wiped away" (Acts 3:17, 19).

So what does that mean for you, baker? Jesus is still the one who makes things new, and the door is open to anyone who turns back to Him. Times of refreshing come from the presence of the Lord (Acts 3:20). I know a little something about being made new, and I'm still not over it. Whatever gifts you have, hand them out in Jesus' name, and let Him get the glory.
